source_text: II. Martianus ait: Responde, cui deo precem fundis? ut ipsi etiam nos sacra reddamus. Achatius dixit: Ego deum meum opto te scire quod prosit et deum qui est verus agnoscere. Martianus ait: Nomen eius mihi enuntia. Achatius dixit: Deus Abraham, deus Isaac et deus Iacob. Martianus ait: Deorum ista sunt nomina? Achatius respondit: Non isti, sed qui locutus est istis, ille est deus verus, illum timere debemus. Martianus ait: Quis est iste? respondit Achatius: Altissimus Adonai, sedens super cherubim et seraphim. Martianus ait: Quid est seraphim? cui Achatius: Altissimi dei minister et excelsae sedis antistes.
thought_title: Naming the God he prays to
orientation: Martianus asks Achatius to name the god he prays for the emperor to, after Achatius said sacrifice is owed to the true God and not to a man.
pass_a_gloss: Martianus said: Answer, to what god do you pour out prayer? so that we also may pay sacred rites to him himself. Achatius said: I desire you to know my God because it may benefit you, and to recognize the God who is true. Martianus said: Declare to me his name. Achatius said: God of Abraham, God of Isaac and God of Jacob. Martianus said: Are these things names of gods? Achatius answered: Not these men themselves, but he who spoke to these men, that one is true God, him we ought to fear. Martianus said: Who is this one? Achatius answered: Most High Adonai, sitting above cherubim and seraphim. Martianus said: What is seraphim? to whom Achatius said: Servant of the Most High God and attendant of the lofty throne.

choices.why: fundis is literally pour, keeping the liquid metaphor rather than general pray
reddere is pay or render what is owed, matching the loyalty-test demand, not merely perform

choices.english: I desire you to know because it may benefit you
choices.why: keeps opto as wish and prosit as subjunctive of benefit, not polished into I want to teach you
rejected: I wish you to know for your own good

choices.term: Non isti, sed qui locutus est istis
choices.english: Not these men themselves, but he who spoke to these men
choices.why: isti are the patriarchs just named, not gods, so the denial must keep the contrast of persons
rejected: Not these, but he who spoke to them

bible_refs.note: quoted source words: Deus Abraham, deus Isaac et deus Iacob

pass_b_english: Martianus said, "Answer me: to which god do you pour out your prayer, so that we may pay sacred rites to him as well?"

Achatius said, "I want you to know my God, because it will do you good, and to acknowledge the God who is the true God." Martianus said, "Speak his name to me." Achatius said, "The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob (Exodus 3:6)."
Martianus said, "Are those the names of gods?" Achatius answered, "Not these men themselves, but the one who spoke to them is the true God, and him we must fear."

Martianus said, "Who is he?" Achatius answered, "The Most High Adonai, enthroned above the cherubim and the seraphim." Martianus said, "What is a seraph?" Achatius told him, "A servant of the Most High God, one who stands before His lofty throne."
